review.limitations: The later sections, all diagram geometry and full crystallographic tables were not independently checked. This is introductory exposition, not an experimental study or a complete wallpaper-group classification.

sections.title: What this pamphlet explains
sections.text: A visual introduction to symmetry of finite objects and repeating patterns, intended for readers without previous crystallography.

sections.title: The useful distinction
sections.text: A symmetry operation moves an object into coincidence with itself. A symmetry element is its geometric reference, such as an axis or mirror plane. Combining operations can force additional symmetries.

sections.title: How the explanation works
sections.text: Teacups and repeated human figures motivate mirror symmetry, rotation and inversion. The text then replaces these pictures with conventional symbols to describe groups compactly.

sections.title: Scope of the classification
sections.text: Crystallographic periodicity restricts rotational orders to 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6; arbitrary isolated objects need not obey that restriction. The pamphlet describes 32 crystallographic point groups.

sections.title: What to try while reading
sections.text: Identify the operation, fixed geometric element and asymmetric unit separately. Check whether the object is finite or periodically repeated before applying crystallographic restrictions.
